blocks.text: Barkpark Tasks · preparation paper 1 of 5 · lane: shell-and-cache · 2026-07-23

content.value: The shell bet: Expo/React Native — and cache-for-instant-open

Four candidate shells were argued honestly against this system's own constraints, not generic mobile lore. The evidence decides: Barkpark Tasks should be an Expo/React Native app whose data layer is @barkpark/core running unmodified (three small injections through the client's existing fetch hook), whose chat and task surfaces are native, and whose paper reader is a WebView hosting the canonical string-emitting renderer — inheriting the byte-parity proof and 80% of the block vocabulary for free. PWA and native Swift/Kotlin are refuted for v1, each on specific evidence. One gate stands before the recommendation hardens: a measured day-1 WebView spike on real Android hardware.

content.value: The verdict

Expo/React Native (Expo SDK 56/57 line, RN 0.85–0.86). Data layer: @barkpark/core as-is — createClient({ fetch: expoFetch }) via the existing config.fetch override (types.ts:114), plus a URL polyfill and a UTF-8 TextDecoder polyfill for Hermes. Chat and tasks: native RN screens. Papers: a full-screen react-native-webview that owns its own scroll, loading renderPortableDocument() string HTML via a local-file baseUrl (never inline source.html) skinned by paper-surface.css (80,451 bytes, already shipped as an @barkpark/react asset). Login: reuse the ratified RFC-8628 device flow + fleet auto-pick cascade from the bp-login-ux charter — the mobile app becomes its fourth consumer after CLI, wizard, and TUI. Migration story runs both directions: the WebView renderer is shell-portable (a PWA can be added later behind the same interface), and a native prose fast-path is the prepared fallback if the WebView spike janks.

Three load-bearing discoveries make this nearly a transcription rather than a build. First, @barkpark/core is genuinely runtime-agnostic and injectable: its SSE transport deliberately avoids EventSource (which cannot carry Authorization) in favor of fetch() + ReadableStream with Last-Event-ID resume, backoff+jitter, and a 75-second idle watchdog — and its entire runtime surface beyond fetch is TextDecoder('utf-8'), URL, AbortController, and an optional crypto.getRandomValues with a Math.random fallback. Second, the “does @barkpark/react run in React Native?” question dissolves: PortableDoc is a pure string emitter — renderPortableDocument() is exported framework-free, byte-parity proven against the Elixir golden for 42 non-plugin types, and one stylesheet skins it. Third, the server already prescribes the mobile lifecycle: chat rows carry seq and replay via Last-Event-ID, live deltas are ephemeral by design with reconnect-and-refetch-at-turn-boundary as the documented recovery, and tasks expose a pull keyset feed that is a ready-made cache invalidator for an app that wakes intermittently. The system was accidentally built for this.

content.value: PWA is refuted as the v1 vehicle on four grounds, each independently sufficient to break a wish-level promise: iOS storage for installed web apps is heuristic and best-effort (same origin quota as a browser tab, smaller disk ceiling, persist() realistically grantable only after install), so “cache for instant open” cannot be guaranteed; Web Push is install-gated, has no silent push, and loses subscriptions in practice; SSE and all JS die within seconds of backgrounding with no standalone-mode exemption; and — found by this run, previously unpinned — the CORS layer gives /v1/chat/* and /v1/tasks/* no per-app allow-list at all, only a blunt instance-wide DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS env var (dataset-scoped cors_origins exists only for /v1/data-shaped paths). Native Swift/Kotlin is refuted more simply: zero reuse of the typed client, the renderer, or the parity harness — everything rebuilt, forever drifting. The react-native-web inversion (one RN codebase emitting a web app too) is mature in 2026 and stays open as a later web story; it does not change the v1 call.

WebView performance on long papers (the 91-block showcase deck) is unprovable by reading — no published benchmark exists for this exact shape. Known physics: Android WebView scroll collapses in the co-scroll-inside-a-native-ScrollView pattern (react-native-webview#17) and inline source.html has a hard content ceiling (#3126) — both avoided by design here (full-screen WebView owning its own scroll; baseUrl file load). Day-1 spike, real hardware, measured: (1) cold-load + frame drops on Android for a real ~100-block paper + the 80 KB paper-surface.css; (2) memory holding 3-4 WebViews warm in a navigation stack; (3) inline vs file-load delta. If it janks, the native prose fast-path (paragraph/heading/list/code — 78% of the corpus by measured usage) promotes from v2 contingency to v1 and the renderer cost roughly doubles. That is the single biggest cost fork in this plan.

blocks.title: The one gate before the recommendation hardens

content.value: What we will create

One Expo app, three surfaces, one typed client, one cache. The login screen is the ratified device-flow cascade; the data layer is @barkpark/core with per-server credentials injected; each surface renders from the local cache first and reconciles against the live feeds. All writes require connectivity (interview truth); the server-side sync/ machinery (sync_cursors, push cursors, CAS pusher) is a server-to-server mirror daemon and is deliberately not touched — its cursor/echo-dedup design is the documented blueprint if offline writes ever come.

blocks.caption: The v1 architecture. Everything inside the app box is new; everything outside already exists and is proven live. The per-server bearer for a plain team member is the identity-cascade lane's build — the one hard server dependency this lane has.

content.value: The data-layer skeleton is a transcription of facts established in this run. The client boots with the last-known location from MMKV, renders each surface from SQLite instantly, then reconciles: tasks replay GET /v1/tasks/events?since=cursor (id-ASC keyset, ≤500/page, stable monotonic cursor); papers ride the same per-dataset SSE stream as tasks — /v1/data/listen/:dataset streams ALL document types, so one stream invalidates both surfaces wherever they share a dataset; chat resumes per-session via Last-Event-ID = seq and obeys the server's own reconnect-and-refetch-at-turn-boundary doctrine on every foreground or network flap.

content.value: Sibling lanes assumed chat transcripts render as PortableDoc blocks through the one shared renderer; this lane recommends native RN rendering. Evidence both ways, honestly: chat rows dual-carry blocks AND source_markdown (chat_controller.ex:1134-1169), so native is safe; all 6 chat-* block families already have full three-surface renderer parity, so the shared-renderer path is also safe. This lane's ruling: the transcript list must be a virtualized native list — per-row WebViews cannot deliver “chat EXCELLENTLY” (keyboard avoidance, 60fps scroll, selection, haptics) — with assistant prose from source_markdown and the six structured row families (tool-diff, todo, thinking, approval, question, plan) as six small native components. The drift surface is bounded (6 families, each with an existing golden to test against), unlike papers (82 types), which is exactly why papers get the WebView and chat does not. The crown paper should ratify or overturn this in one place.

blocks.title: Fork to rule once at the crown: chat transcript rendering

items.value: In v1:

device-flow login + auto-select cascade with cached last location; native tasks; native chat with live SSE; WebView paper reader with offline cached reading; instant cold-open from cache; online-only writes.
Decide at the crown:

push notifications. Three lanes disagree on timing; the factual ground is settled — scc-w13-notify-channels is Web Push + webhook only, so native APNs/FCM push is 100% greenfield server-side work either way. It is the strongest RN-only argument and the largest hidden server cost.
Out of v1, two doors sketched:

paper editing. Door A (cheap, respectable v2): prose-only patch-block against the existing 5-op/ifRev-CAS HTTP surface, unblocked by a surgical auth-seam PR (the ops route today admits only the shared ingest secret or an admin token; Tenancy.Auth already models :write for user principals — see the editing inventory in the coverage appendix). Door B: a WebView hosting the Studio LiveView editor, coupling to browser-session auth. Nothing found makes editing cheap in v1; the wish's “eventually editing” ambition is honored by keeping Door A's seam explicitly in the epic backlog.
Explicitly not v1:

pdrender-wasm as a render path (2.93 MB gzip, Hermes has no wasm — at most a later “view as terminal art” toggle inside the same WebView, exactly as Studio does today); the 15 missing JS block emitters (schema-field family — port only if the corpus census shows real prevalence); react-native-web output; offline writes.

content.value: What we learned
The storm confirmed the emerging shape and corrected it in five places. The findings that carry the decision, including the premises that fell:

items.value: The client was built for injection.

listen.ts avoids EventSource on purpose (no Authorization support) and uses fetch + ReadableStream; config.fetch (types.ts:114) is a public override consumed at listen.ts:166 and transport.ts:288. Edge-detection cannot false-positive in RN. crypto.subtle appears only in the webhook-verify path an app never touches.
The renderer question dissolved.

PortableDoc.tsx is one div + dangerouslySetInnerHTML over renderBlocks(); renderPortableDocument() is exported with no React at all. Byte-parity vs the Elixir golden is CI-pinned for 42 non-plugin types; the test suite pins the registry at exactly 66 keys.
The renderer matrix, counted programmatically:

JS 66 · Elixir 75 canonical (+6 drift aliases = 81) · Go 82 (+1 internal kind). The 15 types missing from JS are entirely arrayOf/codelist/composite/localizedText/embed + the 10 field-* atoms — no prose, media, dataviz, task, or chat block is missing. “dashboard” exists only in the Go TUI registry, nowhere else. Chat: 6/6 on all three surfaces.
One stream invalidates everything.

/v1/data/listen/:dataset carries ALL document-type mutations (no type filter anywhere in listen_controller.ex) — papers and tasks share one invalidation feed. The tasks pull feed (/v1/tasks/events, plain JSON keyset) is the wake-up reconciler. Chat live deltas are ephemeral by doctrine; recovery is reconnect + refetch settled truth (chat_controller.ex:53-60).
Premise fallen — CORS.

A browser client was quietly assumed viable; it is not, today. DatasetCors (endpoint.ex:95) gives dataset-scoped allow-lists only to /v1/data-shaped paths; /v1/chat/* and /v1/tasks/* fall to a global env var. A PWA needs either an instance-wide CORS grant or a new per-app knob — a real, previously unpinned gap.
Premise fallen — iOS PWA hopes.

Installed PWAs get the SAME storage quota as a tab and a smaller disk ceiling (WebKit's own policy post); persist() is heuristic; Web Push is install-only with no silent push; JS suspends seconds after backgrounding, standalone or not; Apple already demonstrated (Feb-Mar 2024 DMA reversal) it will yank PWA capability on short notice. “Cache for instant open” survives on iOS PWA only conditionally — not contractually.
Premise fallen — the SSE library.

No RN SSE library is needed at all: expo/fetch streams since SDK 52 and @barkpark/core's listen.ts IS the SSE parser. Hermes still needs a TextDecoder polyfill (hermes#1403; TextEncoder is native). Current Expo line: SDK 56 (RN 0.85, May 2026) / SDK 57 changelog (RN 0.86, June 2026) — the index page and changelog disagree on “current”; re-check before pinning.
Premise corrected — the stylesheet.

A probe measured 186 KB for cloud/priv/static/app.css; that is the Cloud SPA stylesheet, not the paper skin. The WebView ships api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css — 80,451 bytes, already distributed as an @barkpark/react asset, and as of PR #5651 covering all 18 previously-unstyled block families (that gap is CLOSED on origin/main, with a compose-time coverage gate from #5656).
Android WebView has a known trap with a known dodge.

Co-scrolling a WebView inside a native ScrollView collapses Android scroll perf (react-native-webview#17); inline source.html white-screens above ~20 MB (#3126). The design avoids both by construction: full-screen WebView owning its own scroll, file/baseUrl loading. Still unmeasured for the exact BP shape — hence the day-1 spike gate.
App Store risk is low, verbatim.

Guideline 4.8 exempts apps that “exclusively use your company's own account setup and sign-in systems” — Cloud-only login does not trigger Sign in with Apple. 4.2 passes because the app has three substantive native surfaces (this is itself an argument against a bare-WebView shell). Constraint accepted into the design: all billing/upsell stays strictly web-side to stay clear of 3.1.1.
Greenfield, confirmed twice.

No prior mobile/PWA/RN/Expo art exists in the bp corpus or the repo (six searches + full-tree grep — the only hit is an unrelated transitive npm peer dep). No service worker or manifest in web/. No APNs/FCM anywhere. The login cascade, however, is NOT greenfield: the bp-login-ux charter's device flow + fleet auto-pick (n==1 fast path) is ratified and shipped — reuse it verbatim.
Two adjacent walls belong to sibling lanes but shape this one.

(a) A plain Cloud team member has NO path to a portable data-plane bearer today — credentials reveal is team-admin-gated, studio-link mints only a browser cookie, chat-token mint requires instance owner/admin. The identity lane owns the fix; this lane's cache/client design just stores whatever per-server bearer the cascade yields. (b) Paper-embedded images are bare unsigned /media/files/ paths and a WebView cannot attach a Bearer header — public-visibility media works, token/private media silently 403s. Flagged in-repo already (studio_chat.ex:2441-2442 routed chat attachments AROUND the media plugin for exactly this leak-class).
Housekeeping finding:

@barkpark/core's committed dist/ measures ~21.3/21.7 KB gzip against its own 15.5/16.25 KB size-limit budgets — either the artifact or the budget file is stale; check whether the js size gate is red on main before the epic builds on it.

content.value: Auth today. Cloud login is an RFC-8628-shaped device flow over plain HTTP JSON — POST /v1/auth/device/start (unauthed) → {device_code, user_code, verification_uri, interval:5, expires_in:600}; /poll returns {token, team_id} byte-identical to normal login (cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/device_auth.ex; charter decisions 1-10, 19-25 incl. the n==1 auto-select fast path — the wish's cascade, already ratified and shipped for the CLI). From there the credential chain narrows hard: GET /v1/barkparks/:id/credentials is team-admin-gated server-side (cloud router.ex:1848-1850) and reveals a root admin token; POST .../studio-link works for any member but mints only a 60-second ticket consumed into a browser session cookie, never a JSON bearer (api session_controller.ex); the workspace chat-token mint (POST /w/:ws/p/:proj/v1/chat/tokens, permissions hardcoded ["chat"], D48) sits behind :scoped_admin. A plain member on a phone can obtain no portable data-plane bearer — the identity lane's endpoint (a JSON-bearer sibling of mint_studio_link, scoped to the picked workspace) is the missing piece this app's login flow will consume.

Reading and editing today. The public paper reader is a LiveView (live("/papers/:slug", BulldocsLive) under the Bulldocs plugin) whose disconnected mount returns full server-rendered HTML — but the mobile reader does not scrape it; it renders cached blocks JSON locally through the same string emitter. Media inside papers: src values are bare unsigned /media/files/<path> strings (media/assets.ex:192); GET /media/files/*path is public by default, gated only for token/private visibility, satisfiable in a WebView only via a signed query param nothing currently produces at render time (media/storage/access.ex). Editing: the Studio editor's transport is LiveView pushEvent (paper_editor.ex phx-hooks → Content.apply_paper_block_op(s) in-process) — unreachable off-browser; the HTTP twin POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers/:slug/ops carries 5 op kinds with atomic ops[] and ifRev CAS→412 (bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex:78, :292-335) but its plug (require_ingest_token.ex) admits only the shared ingest secret or an admin token. Tenancy.Auth already models :write for user principals — the auth seam for mobile editing v2 is a surgical plug widen, not a new system.

content.value: Placement judgment, left open deliberately: an Expo app inside js/ joins the pnpm/changesets/size-budget regime built for published npm packages — an app is not a package, and EAS build metadata sits awkwardly there. apps/mobile at the repo root keeps the app's CI shape independent while still consuming @barkpark/core and @barkpark/react as ordinary workspace deps. Lean apps/mobile; the crown decides.
Risks and unknowns

(1) WebView long-paper performance is unmeasured for this exact shape — the day-1 spike is a hard gate, and its failure mode (native prose fast-path promoted to v1) roughly doubles renderer cost. (2) The member-credential gap: until the identity lane ships a member-reachable workspace-scoped bearer mint, this app works only for team admins — the cascade UX is ratified but the credential it must yield does not exist. (3) Push: undecided across lanes, 100% greenfield server-side, and the strongest RN-only advantage — deciding it late risks either shipping a silent chat app or bolting on a new subsystem mid-epic.

items.value: Fourth-surface parity economics: TUI, Studio, and web already demand parity gates; native chat/task screens will drift without their own golden-style gates. The WebView paper choice minimizes this (papers ride the canonical renderer + coverage gate); chat's 6 native components need a small parity harness against the existing chat-block goldens.
Expo SDK churn: the SDK 56/57 “current stable” discrepancy is unresolved (index page vs changelog, fetched the same session); pin the SDK at epic start, budget one upgrade per quarter.

Media in the WebView: token/private-visibility images silently 403 (bare unsigned src, no header injection for sub-resources). Fine while paper media stays default-public; a render-time signed src or fetch-to-blob shim is required the day scoped/private papers carry media. Whether that corpus exists in production today was NOT verified — a live landmine of unknown reality.
The 15 missing JS block types degrade to an explicit Unsupported placeholder in the WebView; corpus prevalence of those types was not measured. Cheap census before deciding to port.
@barkpark/core dist/ vs size-limit budget mismatch — determine whether the js size gate is currently red on main before building on it.

App Store: low risk as shaped, but the OTA-update three-condition folklore (‘3.3.2’) could not be verified at primary source — it lives in the private developer agreement; keep OTA pushes to fixes, never hidden features.
External-physics facts (iOS PWA policy, Expo versions, WebView issue reports) are web-sourced and demoted where no rerun exists — re-verify citations at epic start; policies move.
Left to the user/crown:

how much premium input feel matters vs shipping speed (the last honest argument PWA retains); push in v1, v1.5, or later; chat-transcript rendering fork (this lane says native — ratify once); app placement (apps/mobile vs js/); which editing door (prose-only ops seam vs LiveView WebView) gets filed as the v2 opener; whether to fund the 15-emitter port or accept placeholders.

content.value: The system was accidentally built for this: an injectable client, a string-emitting renderer with a byte-parity proof, and a server that already teaches its clients how to sleep and wake. The epic's first commit is a transcription, not a debate.

Written by the shell-and-cache lane of the Barkpark Tasks preparation run (2026-07-23): one lane investigation over origin/main + the bp corpus, hardened by ten storm probes (renderer matrix counted programmatically and CI-cross-pinned; streaming census read from controller source; credential map traced mint-by-mint; external physics web-cited, with no-rerun facts explicitly demoted). Facts carry file:line anchors on origin/main; the local checkout was verifiably stale during the run and was never trusted over git show. This is one of five lane papers; the crown paper — barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone — combines all five and rules the cross-lane forks named here (chat rendering, push timing, token strategy vs editing, tenancy depth of the cascade). Nothing was built this run; the repo was read-only throughout.

blocks.title: Method, provenance, and where this paper goes next

body_html:
Barkpark Tasks · preparation paper 1 of 5 · lane: shell-and-cache · 2026-07-23

The shell bet: Expo/React Native — and cache-for-instant-open

Four candidate shells were argued honestly against this system's own constraints, not generic mobile lore. The evidence decides: Barkpark Tasks should be an Expo/React Native app whose data layer is @barkpark/core running unmodified (three small injections through the client's existing fetch hook), whose chat and task surfaces are native, and whose paper reader is a WebView hosting the canonical string-emitting renderer — inheriting the byte-parity proof and 80% of the block vocabulary for free. PWA and native Swift/Kotlin are refuted for v1, each on specific evidence. One gate stands before the recommendation hardens: a measured day-1 WebView spike on real Android hardware.

Shell scorecard · 66/82 renderer matrix · SSE per shell · Cache architecture · Data-layer skeleton · Day-1 spikes

66/82
block types the JS renderer covers of the three-surface union — a WebView reader inherits 80% for free, and the 15-type gap is entirely the schema-field family
~21 KB
gzip for the whole @barkpark/core typed client including SSE listen() — it runs under Expo with a fetch injection and two polyfills
6/6
chat block families already at full three-surface renderer parity — the mobile chat view has zero renderer-parity risk
2.93 MB
gzip of the pdrender-wasm TUI renderer — real, working, and strictly an opt-in toggle, never the primary reading path
§
  1. The verdict
  2. What we will create
  3. What we learned
  4. How the system works today
  5. Files likely to change
  6. Risks and unknowns
  7. Coverage appendix

The verdict

Recommendation Expo/React Native (Expo SDK 56/57 line, RN 0.85–0.86). Data layer: @barkpark/core as-is — createClient({ fetch: expoFetch }) via the existing config.fetch override (types.ts:114), plus a URL polyfill and a UTF-8 TextDecoder polyfill for Hermes. Chat and tasks: native RN screens. Papers: a full-screen react-native-webview that owns its own scroll, loading renderPortableDocument() string HTML via a local-file baseUrl (never inline source.html) skinned by paper-surface.css (80,451 bytes, already shipped as an @barkpark/react asset). Login: reuse the ratified RFC-8628 device flow + fleet auto-pick cascade from the bp-login-ux charter — the mobile app becomes its fourth consumer after CLI, wizard, and TUI. Migration story runs both directions: the WebView renderer is shell-portable (a PWA can be added later behind the same interface), and a native prose fast-path is the prepared fallback if the WebView spike janks.

Three load-bearing discoveries make this nearly a transcription rather than a build. First, @barkpark/core is genuinely runtime-agnostic and injectable: its SSE transport deliberately avoids EventSource (which cannot carry Authorization) in favor of fetch() + ReadableStream with Last-Event-ID resume, backoff+jitter, and a 75-second idle watchdog — and its entire runtime surface beyond fetch is TextDecoder('utf-8'), URL, AbortController, and an optional crypto.getRandomValues with a Math.random fallback. Second, the “does @barkpark/react run in React Native?” question dissolves: PortableDoc is a pure string emitter — renderPortableDocument() is exported framework-free, byte-parity proven against the Elixir golden for 42 non-plugin types, and one stylesheet skins it. Third, the server already prescribes the mobile lifecycle: chat rows carry seq and replay via Last-Event-ID, live deltas are ephemeral by design with reconnect-and-refetch-at-turn-boundary as the documented recovery, and tasks expose a pull keyset feed that is a ready-made cache invalidator for an app that wakes intermittently. The system was accidentally built for this.

DimensionExpo/React NativePWANative Swift/Kotlin
@barkpark/core reuse (client + SSE)Full — fetch injection + 2 polyfills; listen() unmodifiedFull, zero shimsNone — full client rewrite
PortableDoc papersWebView string HTML — inherits 66 types + parity proofSame renderer, native DOMRebuild ~66 emitters + re-express 80 KB CSS; permanent drift risk
SSE live chat incl. backgroundingexpo/fetch streams (SDK 52+); reconnect on foreground, native lifecycle hooksSuspended within seconds of backgrounding; restore sometimes forces reloadNative URLSession/OkHttp — fine, but bespoke framing code
Instant-open cacheMMKV + SQLite, fully ownediOS storage best-effort (persist() heuristic, 15%/20% quota); eviction riskFully owned
Push notificationsAPNs/FCM path exists (greenfield server-side either way)Install-only Web Push, no silent push, lossy subscriptionsAPNs/FCM native
CORS exposureNone — not a browserBlocked on /v1/chat/* and /v1/tasks/* today; only a global env-var knob existsNone
DistributionApp Store review — low risk (4.8 exemption applies); EAS + OTA JS updatesZero review, instant updates, but manual-install funnel shrinks reach 10-15xApp Store; slowest iteration
Chat input feel (keyboard, haptics, share sheet)NativeBrowser-grade; the weak flank for “chat EXCELLENTLY”Native, best-in-class
Cost / maintenanceOne codebase; joins the JS regime; 4th surface parity to mindCheapest to shipTwo codebases, zero reuse — most expensive

PWA is refuted as the v1 vehicle on four grounds, each independently sufficient to break a wish-level promise: iOS storage for installed web apps is heuristic and best-effort (same origin quota as a browser tab, smaller disk ceiling, persist() realistically grantable only after install), so “cache for instant open” cannot be guaranteed; Web Push is install-gated, has no silent push, and loses subscriptions in practice; SSE and all JS die within seconds of backgrounding with no standalone-mode exemption; and — found by this run, previously unpinned — the CORS layer gives /v1/chat/* and /v1/tasks/* no per-app allow-list at all, only a blunt instance-wide DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS env var (dataset-scoped cors_origins exists only for /v1/data-shaped paths). Native Swift/Kotlin is refuted more simply: zero reuse of the typed client, the renderer, or the parity harness — everything rebuilt, forever drifting. The react-native-web inversion (one RN codebase emitting a web app too) is mature in 2026 and stays open as a later web story; it does not change the v1 call.

The one gate before the recommendation hardens WebView performance on long papers (the 91-block showcase deck) is unprovable by reading — no published benchmark exists for this exact shape. Known physics: Android WebView scroll collapses in the co-scroll-inside-a-native-ScrollView pattern (react-native-webview#17) and inline source.html has a hard content ceiling (#3126) — both avoided by design here (full-screen WebView owning its own scroll; baseUrl file load). Day-1 spike, real hardware, measured: (1) cold-load + frame drops on Android for a real ~100-block paper + the 80 KB paper-surface.css; (2) memory holding 3-4 WebViews warm in a navigation stack; (3) inline vs file-load delta. If it janks, the native prose fast-path (paragraph/heading/list/code — 78% of the corpus by measured usage) promotes from v2 contingency to v1 and the renderer cost roughly doubles. That is the single biggest cost fork in this plan.

What we will create

One Expo app, three surfaces, one typed client, one cache. The login screen is the ratified device-flow cascade; the data layer is @barkpark/core with per-server credentials injected; each surface renders from the local cache first and reconciles against the live feeds. All writes require connectivity (interview truth); the server-side sync/ machinery (sync_cursors, push cursors, CAS pusher) is a server-to-server mirror daemon and is deliberately not touched — its cursor/echo-dedup design is the documented blueprint if offline writes ever come.

The data-layer skeleton is a transcription of facts established in this run. The client boots with the last-known location from MMKV, renders each surface from SQLite instantly, then reconciles: tasks replay GET /v1/tasks/events?since=cursor (id-ASC keyset, ≤500/page, stable monotonic cursor); papers ride the same per-dataset SSE stream as tasks — /v1/data/listen/:dataset streams ALL document types, so one stream invalidates both surfaces wherever they share a dataset; chat resumes per-session via Last-Event-ID = seq and obeys the server's own reconnect-and-refetch-at-turn-boundary doctrine on every foreground or network flap.

// apps/mobile/src/data/client.ts — the epic's first architectural commit
import { fetch as expoFetch } from 'expo/fetch'      // WinterCG fetch, streams since SDK 52
import '@bacons/text-decoder/install'                 // Hermes still lacks TextDecoder (hermes#1403)
import 'react-native-url-polyfill/auto'               // URL
import { createClient } from '@barkpark/core'

export function makeClient(server: SavedServer) {
  return createClient({
    baseUrl: server.url,
    token: server.bearer,          // per-server credential from the login cascade
    fetch: expoFetch as unknown as typeof globalThis.fetch, // config.fetch hook, types.ts:114
  })
}

// listen.ts's SSE framing (Last-Event-ID, backoff+jitter, 75s idle watchdog)
// now runs verbatim under Hermes — no react-native-sse, no fetch-event-source.
StoreHoldsInvalidated byStaleness UX
MMKV (key-value, sync)Last location cascade (server → workspace → project → dataset), per-feed cursors, device-flow tokenOverwritten on navigation / loginAuto-select cascades exactly as the wish describes; selection screen always reachable
SQLite: tasksTask rows per dataset (list + detail fields)Foreground replay of /v1/tasks/events?since=cursor; live task.* events on /v1/data/listen while openRender cached instantly; sync badge until the replay settles
SQLite: papersPortableDoc blocks JSON per paper (render on read in the WebView)mutation events with type=paper on the same /v1/data/listen stream; refetch docs whose rev changedCached read always available offline; badge on stale rev
SQLite: chatTranscript rows keyed (session_id, seq) incl. blocks + source_markdownLast-Event-ID=seq replay on reconnect; settled-truth refetch at turn boundary per the server's doctrineTranscript instant; live deltas stream only while foregrounded
Fork to rule once at the crown: chat transcript rendering Sibling lanes assumed chat transcripts render as PortableDoc blocks through the one shared renderer; this lane recommends native RN rendering. Evidence both ways, honestly: chat rows dual-carry blocks AND source_markdown (chat_controller.ex:1134-1169), so native is safe; all 6 chat-* block families already have full three-surface renderer parity, so the shared-renderer path is also safe. This lane's ruling: the transcript list must be a virtualized native list — per-row WebViews cannot deliver “chat EXCELLENTLY” (keyboard avoidance, 60fps scroll, selection, haptics) — with assistant prose from source_markdown and the six structured row families (tool-diff, todo, thinking, approval, question, plan) as six small native components. The drift surface is bounded (6 families, each with an existing golden to test against), unlike papers (82 types), which is exactly why papers get the WebView and chat does not. The crown paper should ratify or overturn this in one place.
  • In v1: device-flow login + auto-select cascade with cached last location; native tasks; native chat with live SSE; WebView paper reader with offline cached reading; instant cold-open from cache; online-only writes.
  • Decide at the crown: push notifications. Three lanes disagree on timing; the factual ground is settled — scc-w13-notify-channels is Web Push + webhook only, so native APNs/FCM push is 100% greenfield server-side work either way. It is the strongest RN-only argument and the largest hidden server cost.
  • Out of v1, two doors sketched: paper editing. Door A (cheap, respectable v2): prose-only patch-block against the existing 5-op/ifRev-CAS HTTP surface, unblocked by a surgical auth-seam PR (the ops route today admits only the shared ingest secret or an admin token; Tenancy.Auth already models :write for user principals — see the editing inventory in the coverage appendix). Door B: a WebView hosting the Studio LiveView editor, coupling to browser-session auth. Nothing found makes editing cheap in v1; the wish's “eventually editing” ambition is honored by keeping Door A's seam explicitly in the epic backlog.
  • Explicitly not v1: pdrender-wasm as a render path (2.93 MB gzip, Hermes has no wasm — at most a later “view as terminal art” toggle inside the same WebView, exactly as Studio does today); the 15 missing JS block emitters (schema-field family — port only if the corpus census shows real prevalence); react-native-web output; offline writes.
§

What we learned

The storm confirmed the emerging shape and corrected it in five places. The findings that carry the decision, including the premises that fell:

  • The client was built for injection. listen.ts avoids EventSource on purpose (no Authorization support) and uses fetch + ReadableStream; config.fetch (types.ts:114) is a public override consumed at listen.ts:166 and transport.ts:288. Edge-detection cannot false-positive in RN. crypto.subtle appears only in the webhook-verify path an app never touches.
  • The renderer question dissolved. PortableDoc.tsx is one div + dangerouslySetInnerHTML over renderBlocks(); renderPortableDocument() is exported with no React at all. Byte-parity vs the Elixir golden is CI-pinned for 42 non-plugin types; the test suite pins the registry at exactly 66 keys.
  • The renderer matrix, counted programmatically: JS 66 · Elixir 75 canonical (+6 drift aliases = 81) · Go 82 (+1 internal kind). The 15 types missing from JS are entirely arrayOf/codelist/composite/localizedText/embed + the 10 field-* atoms — no prose, media, dataviz, task, or chat block is missing. “dashboard” exists only in the Go TUI registry, nowhere else. Chat: 6/6 on all three surfaces.
  • One stream invalidates everything. /v1/data/listen/:dataset carries ALL document-type mutations (no type filter anywhere in listen_controller.ex) — papers and tasks share one invalidation feed. The tasks pull feed (/v1/tasks/events, plain JSON keyset) is the wake-up reconciler. Chat live deltas are ephemeral by doctrine; recovery is reconnect + refetch settled truth (chat_controller.ex:53-60).
  • Premise fallen — CORS. A browser client was quietly assumed viable; it is not, today. DatasetCors (endpoint.ex:95) gives dataset-scoped allow-lists only to /v1/data-shaped paths; /v1/chat/* and /v1/tasks/* fall to a global env var. A PWA needs either an instance-wide CORS grant or a new per-app knob — a real, previously unpinned gap.
  • Premise fallen — iOS PWA hopes. Installed PWAs get the SAME storage quota as a tab and a smaller disk ceiling (WebKit's own policy post); persist() is heuristic; Web Push is install-only with no silent push; JS suspends seconds after backgrounding, standalone or not; Apple already demonstrated (Feb-Mar 2024 DMA reversal) it will yank PWA capability on short notice. “Cache for instant open” survives on iOS PWA only conditionally — not contractually.
  • Premise fallen — the SSE library. No RN SSE library is needed at all: expo/fetch streams since SDK 52 and @barkpark/core's listen.ts IS the SSE parser. Hermes still needs a TextDecoder polyfill (hermes#1403; TextEncoder is native). Current Expo line: SDK 56 (RN 0.85, May 2026) / SDK 57 changelog (RN 0.86, June 2026) — the index page and changelog disagree on “current”; re-check before pinning.
  • Premise corrected — the stylesheet. A probe measured 186 KB for cloud/priv/static/app.css; that is the Cloud SPA stylesheet, not the paper skin. The WebView ships api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css — 80,451 bytes, already distributed as an @barkpark/react asset, and as of PR #5651 covering all 18 previously-unstyled block families (that gap is CLOSED on origin/main, with a compose-time coverage gate from #5656).
  • Android WebView has a known trap with a known dodge. Co-scrolling a WebView inside a native ScrollView collapses Android scroll perf (react-native-webview#17); inline source.html white-screens above ~20 MB (#3126). The design avoids both by construction: full-screen WebView owning its own scroll, file/baseUrl loading. Still unmeasured for the exact BP shape — hence the day-1 spike gate.
  • App Store risk is low, verbatim. Guideline 4.8 exempts apps that “exclusively use your company's own account setup and sign-in systems” — Cloud-only login does not trigger Sign in with Apple. 4.2 passes because the app has three substantive native surfaces (this is itself an argument against a bare-WebView shell). Constraint accepted into the design: all billing/upsell stays strictly web-side to stay clear of 3.1.1.
  • Greenfield, confirmed twice. No prior mobile/PWA/RN/Expo art exists in the bp corpus or the repo (six searches + full-tree grep — the only hit is an unrelated transitive npm peer dep). No service worker or manifest in web/. No APNs/FCM anywhere. The login cascade, however, is NOT greenfield: the bp-login-ux charter's device flow + fleet auto-pick (n==1 fast path) is ratified and shipped — reuse it verbatim.
  • Two adjacent walls belong to sibling lanes but shape this one. (a) A plain Cloud team member has NO path to a portable data-plane bearer today — credentials reveal is team-admin-gated, studio-link mints only a browser cookie, chat-token mint requires instance owner/admin. The identity lane owns the fix; this lane's cache/client design just stores whatever per-server bearer the cascade yields. (b) Paper-embedded images are bare unsigned /media/files/ paths and a WebView <img> cannot attach a Bearer header — public-visibility media works, token/private media silently 403s. Flagged in-repo already (studio_chat.ex:2441-2442 routed chat attachments AROUND the media plugin for exactly this leak-class).
  • Housekeeping finding: @barkpark/core's committed dist/ measures ~21.3/21.7 KB gzip against its own 15.5/16.25 KB size-limit budgets — either the artifact or the budget file is stale; check whether the js size gate is red on main before the epic builds on it.

How the system works today

The transport table below IS the data layer's specification — the mobile client implements exactly these rows and nothing else. Anchors are file:line on origin/main.

StreamPathAuthCursor / resumeEventsDegrade behavior

Auth today. Cloud login is an RFC-8628-shaped device flow over plain HTTP JSON — POST /v1/auth/device/start (unauthed) → {device_code, user_code, verification_uri, interval:5, expires_in:600}; /poll returns {token, team_id} byte-identical to normal login (cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/device_auth.ex; charter decisions 1-10, 19-25 incl. the n==1 auto-select fast path — the wish's cascade, already ratified and shipped for the CLI). From there the credential chain narrows hard: GET /v1/barkparks/:id/credentials is team-admin-gated server-side (cloud router.ex:1848-1850) and reveals a root admin token; POST .../studio-link works for any member but mints only a 60-second ticket consumed into a browser session cookie, never a JSON bearer (api session_controller.ex); the workspace chat-token mint (POST /w/:ws/p/:proj/v1/chat/tokens, permissions hardcoded ["chat"], D48) sits behind :scoped_admin. A plain member on a phone can obtain no portable data-plane bearer — the identity lane's endpoint (a JSON-bearer sibling of mint_studio_link, scoped to the picked workspace) is the missing piece this app's login flow will consume.

Reading and editing today. The public paper reader is a LiveView (live("/papers/:slug", BulldocsLive) under the Bulldocs plugin) whose disconnected mount returns full server-rendered HTML — but the mobile reader does not scrape it; it renders cached blocks JSON locally through the same string emitter. Media inside papers: src values are bare unsigned /media/files/<path> strings (media/assets.ex:192); GET /media/files/*path is public by default, gated only for token/private visibility, satisfiable in a WebView only via a signed query param nothing currently produces at render time (media/storage/access.ex). Editing: the Studio editor's transport is LiveView pushEvent (paper_editor.ex phx-hooks → Content.apply_paper_block_op(s) in-process) — unreachable off-browser; the HTTP twin POST /v1/plugins/bulldocs/papers/:slug/ops carries 5 op kinds with atomic ops[] and ifRev CAS→412 (bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex:78, :292-335) but its plug (require_ingest_token.ex) admits only the shared ingest secret or an admin token. Tenancy.Auth already models :write for user principals — the auth seam for mobile editing v2 is a surgical plug widen, not a new system.

Files likely to change

PathWhy it changesBlast radius

Placement judgment, left open deliberately: an Expo app inside js/ joins the pnpm/changesets/size-budget regime built for published npm packages — an app is not a package, and EAS build metadata sits awkwardly there. apps/mobile at the repo root keeps the app's CI shape independent while still consuming @barkpark/core and @barkpark/react as ordinary workspace deps. Lean apps/mobile; the crown decides.

Risks and unknowns

Top three, honestly (1) WebView long-paper performance is unmeasured for this exact shape — the day-1 spike is a hard gate, and its failure mode (native prose fast-path promoted to v1) roughly doubles renderer cost. (2) The member-credential gap: until the identity lane ships a member-reachable workspace-scoped bearer mint, this app works only for team admins — the cascade UX is ratified but the credential it must yield does not exist. (3) Push: undecided across lanes, 100% greenfield server-side, and the strongest RN-only advantage — deciding it late risks either shipping a silent chat app or bolting on a new subsystem mid-epic.
  • Fourth-surface parity economics: TUI, Studio, and web already demand parity gates; native chat/task screens will drift without their own golden-style gates. The WebView paper choice minimizes this (papers ride the canonical renderer + coverage gate); chat's 6 native components need a small parity harness against the existing chat-block goldens.
  • Expo SDK churn: the SDK 56/57 “current stable” discrepancy is unresolved (index page vs changelog, fetched the same session); pin the SDK at epic start, budget one upgrade per quarter.
  • Media in the WebView: token/private-visibility images silently 403 (bare unsigned src, no header injection for sub-resources). Fine while paper media stays default-public; a render-time signed src or fetch-to-blob shim is required the day scoped/private papers carry media. Whether that corpus exists in production today was NOT verified — a live landmine of unknown reality.
  • The 15 missing JS block types degrade to an explicit Unsupported placeholder in the WebView; corpus prevalence of those types was not measured. Cheap census before deciding to port.
  • @barkpark/core dist/ vs size-limit budget mismatch — determine whether the js size gate is currently red on main before building on it.
  • App Store: low risk as shaped, but the OTA-update three-condition folklore (‘3.3.2’) could not be verified at primary source — it lives in the private developer agreement; keep OTA pushes to fixes, never hidden features.
  • External-physics facts (iOS PWA policy, Expo versions, WebView issue reports) are web-sourced and demoted where no rerun exists — re-verify citations at epic start; policies move.
  • Left to the user/crown: how much premium input feel matters vs shipping speed (the last honest argument PWA retains); push in v1, v1.5, or later; chat-transcript rendering fork (this lane says native — ratify once); app placement (apps/mobile vs js/); which editing door (prose-only ops seam vs LiveView WebView) gets filed as the v2 opener; whether to fund the 15-emitter port or accept placeholders.

The system was accidentally built for this: an injectable client, a string-emitting renderer with a byte-parity proof, and a server that already teaches its clients how to sleep and wake. The epic's first commit is a transcription, not a debate.

Method, provenance, and where this paper goes next Written by the shell-and-cache lane of the Barkpark Tasks preparation run (2026-07-23): one lane investigation over origin/main + the bp corpus, hardened by ten storm probes (renderer matrix counted programmatically and CI-cross-pinned; streaming census read from controller source; credential map traced mint-by-mint; external physics web-cited, with no-rerun facts explicitly demoted). Facts carry file:line anchors on origin/main; the local checkout was verifiably stale during the run and was never trusted over git show. This is one of five lane papers; the crown paper — barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone — combines all five and rules the cross-lane forks named here (chat rendering, push timing, token strategy vs editing, tenancy depth of the cascade). Nothing was built this run; the repo was read-only throughout.
description: Preparation paper (lane: shell-and-cache) for the Barkpark Tasks mobile app. The platform decision is made decidable on evidence: Expo/React Native wins, with @barkpark/core run unmodified (three small injections via the existing config.fetch hook), native RN chat and task surfaces, and a WebView paper reader hosting the canonical renderPortableDocument() string emitter + paper-surface.css — inheriting 66 of 82 union block types and the Elixir-golden byte-parity proof for free. PWA is refuted for v1 (iOS storage is best-effort not contractual, push is install-only, SSE dies on backgrounding, and chat/tasks routes have no per-app CORS knob); native Swift/Kotlin is refuted (zero reuse). Cache-for-instant-open = MMKV for the location cascade + cursors, SQLite for tasks/papers/transcripts, invalidated by the tasks keyset pull feed and the type-agnostic per-dataset SSE stream. Includes the streaming-endpoint table, renderer matrix, cache design, data-layer skeleton, day-1 spike gates, files likely to change, and the coverage appendix. Feeds the crown paper barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone.
